definition: A specific type of model drift where the statistical relationship between input features and target outputs changes over time.
details: Concept drift differs from simple data drift (a change in input distribution alone) because the underlying task itself effectively changes, requiring the model's learned mapping to be updated to remain accurate.
story: Picture an engineer at a cluttered workbench, turning a clever idea over in their hands until it finally clicks. At its heart it is a simple notion, once you strip away the fancy name. A small key that opens a much bigger door. It is one of those ideas that feels obvious only after someone shows it to you. That is Concept Drift — a small key that opens a big door.
